chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-'Is ibn Al-Qasim, who said:

“By Allah, there may come upon a man fifty years in which Allah has not accepted from him a single salat (prayer). So what thing is more severe than this? By Allah, indeed you know among your neighbors and your companions one who, if he were to pray for some of you, you would not accept it from him because of his making light of it. Indeed, Allah accepts only what is good, so how would He accept that which has been treated lightly?”

key_terms.أَصْحَابِكُمْ: your companions, referring to associates and close acquaintances
key_terms.الْحَسَنَ: that which is good, sound, and worthy of acceptance
key_terms.اِسْتِخْفَافِهِ: his treating it lightly, showing disregard or lack of due seriousness
key_terms.جِيرَانِكُمْ: your neighbors, indicating familiar people in one's social circle
key_terms.صَلَاةً: salat (prayer), the central act of worship being discussed
key_terms.قَبِلَ: accepted, meaning received by Allah with approval

ai.seo_question: Can a person pray for many years without any salat (prayer) being accepted by Allah?
ai.summary: The hadith warns that a person may spend many years performing salat (prayer) without having even one prayer accepted due to treating it lightly. It emphasizes the gravity of reverence and sincerity in worship, teaching that Allah accepts only what is properly honored and well performed.
